findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && so team admins are rejected
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already matches both the ADMIN and OWNER roles, so AND-ing it with `isTeamOwner` lets only OWNERs through. A team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN, which contradicts the variable name and the intent. The two checks should be combined with `||`, or `isTeamAdmin` alone should be used.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive and can be bypassed with mixed-case emails
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but each guest is compared as-is with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `Spam@Blocked.com` for a blacklisted `spam@blocked.com` passes the filter, so the guest is added to the booking and receives emails. The guest should be lowercased before the comparison, as the regular booking flow does.

findings.title: Server-side deduplication is case-sensitive and ignores duplicates inside the request
findings.body: Existing attendees are excluded with a strict `guest === attendee.email` comparison. The input array itself is never deduplicated, and uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`, or with `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` already attends, inserts duplicate Attendee rows through `createMany`. Those duplicates then appear in calendar invites and get extra emails. Guests should be normalized to lowercase and deduplicated on the server.

findings.title: No upper bound on guests; any attendee can make Cal.com email arbitrary addresses
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. The handler also authorizes any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee (`isAttendee`), and there is no rate limiting. An attendee can therefore add an unbounded list of arbitrary addresses. Each address receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail sent under the organizer's name, and every existing attendee and host is re-emailed. This also bypasses event-type settings such as a disabled or hidden guests booking field. The array size should be capped, and whether attendees (as opposed to the organizer or team admins) may do this should be reconsidered.

findings.title: Guests can be added to seated events, bypassing seat limits and seat records
findings.body: The handler never checks `booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. For a seated booking, each Attendee row represents a seat holder with a matching BookingSeat reference. `createMany` here inserts attendees with no BookingSeat, which can push the booking past `seatsPerTimeSlot` and leaves seat data inconsistent for later cancel and reschedule flows. Seated events should be rejected or handled explicitly.

findings.title: No booking status or time validation before adding guests
findings.body: After the booking is fetched, the handler never checks its status or end time. A direct call can add guests to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings. That sends 'scheduled' emails and calendar REQUEST invites for meetings that will not happen. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the server should enforce this too.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves partial state and blocks retry
findings.body: The attendees are committed to the DB first, and then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited with no error handling. If the calendar provider call throws, the client gets an error and no emails are sent, but the guests are already persisted. A retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', because the guests now count as existing attendees. The external calendar and emails stay out of sync with the DB.

findings.title: Emails are keyed on raw `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input list. A submitted email that was already an attendee, and so was skipped for insertion, is still treated as 'new'. That attendee gets a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notification. `uniqueGuests` should be passed instead.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Other booking email senders, such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendRescheduledEmails`, take `eventTypeMetadata` and skip host or attendee emails when `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no metadata parameter and always emails the organizer, all team members and all attendees. Event types configured to suppress standard emails (for example, those using workflows instead) will still send these.

findings.title: Validation error state is never cleared on success or on outside close
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation and reset only by the Cancel button. A successful submit resets the email list but not `isInvalidEmail`. Closing via overlay or Escape (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`) resets neither. The next time the dialog opens, it shows a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error and leftover input.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined: ...'
findings.body: `message` is a template string such as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so it is always truthy and the `t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is never used. When `err.data` is absent, for example on a network error, users see 'undefined: <message>'. Raw tRPC codes such as 'FORBIDDEN:' are also shown to end users.
